title: Biblical Syncretism Dossiers — Wave 32 Specialist Atlas Promotions
purpose: Promote high-value findings from specialist Access/House/Stone, Adam/Seed/Garden/Farm, Circle/Boundary/Return and Angel/Eye/Sprout atlases into the active Bible corpus while preserving anti-flattening controls and role boundaries.

new_relations.project_anchor: The project joins Father, Son, Spirit, Door/access, House, citizenship, cornerstone and living-building imagery; the specialist atlas identified Ephesians 2 as an unusually dense single-passage microcosm.
new_relations.source_direction: Project House/Access architecture first; Ephesians 2 whole-passage synthesis later.
new_relations.boundary: Ephesians centers reconciliation in Christ and access through Christ in one Spirit to the Father; it does not identify Tim as Father, Christ or cornerstone.

biblical_sequence: access to Father through Christ in Spirit
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Ephesians 2 is a high-density structural comparator for reconciliation→access→household→dwelling while preserving Trinitarian role distribution.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It makes reconciliation and outsider-to-household movement central tests of any project House theology.

new_relations.project_anchor: Project anchor/leash analysis previously leaned toward tethering and constraint; the specialist atlas identified Hebrews 6 as a positive anchor whose relation reaches toward a destination beyond a sacred boundary.
new_relations.source_direction: Project tether/anchor topology first; Hebrews positive-anchor correction later.
new_relations.boundary: The text speaks metaphorically of hope entering the inner sanctuary where Jesus is forerunner/high priest; it is not mechanics or a literal spatial tether.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Hebrews 6 establishes that anchor imagery can stabilize by relation to a future destination rather than by preventing movement.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It forces the project to type anchors by function: restrictive tether, orienting reference or hope/target anchor.

new_relations.project_anchor: Gate, broad-place correction, survival, rejected stone and cornerstone were separate project motifs; Psalm 118 places them in one liturgical sequence.
new_relations.source_direction: Project Gate/rejected-stone vocabulary first; Psalm 118 whole-scene integration later.
new_relations.boundary: Psalm 118's original speaker/context is not simply a modern claimant; later New Testament texts apply the stone image christologically.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Psalm 118 tightly joins life, access and rejected-stone reversal, with later Christian reception centering the stone in Christ.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It makes cornerstone symbolism architectural/community-facing rather than generic 'rejected person becomes important' rhetoric.

new_relations.project_anchor: Older project wording calls Tim a 'caretaker of Adam'; the specialist atlas notes that Genesis presents Adam/humanity as caretaker of the Garden, turning the project phrase into a possible stewardship-of-stewardship structure.
new_relations.source_direction: Project 'caretaker of Adam' wording first; Genesis vocation comparison later.
new_relations.boundary: Genesis 2 does not appoint Tim over Adam or humanity. The strongest comparison is responsibility for protecting humanity's capacity to serve/guard creation, not ownership of people.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Genesis 2 makes caretaker language stewardship-centered and can ethically reinterpret 'caretaker of Adam' as responsibility rather than sovereignty.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It shifts authority from possession to preservation of others' ability to fulfill their own vocation.

new_relations.project_anchor: Project Seed-of-Strife/Farm language can encourage sorting metaphors; the specialist atlas identifies Jesus' wheat-and-weeds parable as crucial restraint against premature uprooting.
new_relations.source_direction: Project seed/sorting language first; Gospel restraint added later.
new_relations.boundary: The parable's eschatological interpretation is Jesus' own narrative framework and does not license modern groups to classify people as weeds, demons or disposable bad seed.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Matthew 13 directly supplies an anti-purge control for mixed-field and bad-seed rhetoric.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It is one of the strongest biblical countertexts against turning symbolic classification into immediate social exclusion or harm.

new_relations.project_anchor: The project uses hidden seeds, hidden rooms and underground life with both shadow and positive meanings; the specialist atlas found that Jesus' parables likewise give hiddenness multiple valences.
new_relations.source_direction: Project hidden-seed vocabulary first; parable comparison later.
new_relations.boundary: The parables use distinct images and should not be merged into one doctrine of secrecy. Hiddenness itself is not proof of goodness or evil.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Matthew 13 demonstrates that hiddenness is morally/functionally neutral until the process and fruit are known.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It protects the project from equating underground, secret or invisible states with either holiness or corruption by default.

new_relations.project_anchor: Farm and Garden are major project poles; the specialist atlas reframes their strongest biblical distinction as extractive versus restorative stewardship rather than simply bad place versus good place.
new_relations.source_direction: Project Farm/Garden polarity first; biblical stewardship synthesis later.
new_relations.boundary: These passages use garden, flock, shepherd, gate and vine images in different contexts; they do not encode the project's Farm mythology literally.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical cultivation imagery supports testing Farm/Garden by stewardship outcomes rather than by label or location alone.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It makes exploitation versus cultivation measurable in terms of whether participants become safer, stronger and more capable.

new_relations.project_anchor: Project Son imagery oscillates between agent, vessel, sacrificed grain and source of continuation; the specialist atlas found biblical seed language where Son imagery can occupy both sower and dying-seed roles.
new_relations.source_direction: Project role oscillation first; biblical double-role synthesis later.
new_relations.boundary: Matthew's Son of Man as sower and John's grain/death saying have distinct contexts; neither identifies the project Son with Jesus by resemblance.

biblical_sequence: Son of Man sows good seed
grain dies and bears much fruit
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical seed grammar allows a figure to function as both sower/agent and seed/death-growth symbol without those roles being identical.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It helps the backend represent role multiplicity without forcing every Son metaphor into one fixed ontology.

new_relations.project_anchor: Project House/rooms and Field/Garden often appear as separate symbolic domains; Matthew 13 moves from public field parable into private house explanation.
new_relations.source_direction: Project House/Field distinction first; narrative relation noticed later.
new_relations.boundary: The house in Matthew 13 is simply the setting of explanation; it should not be overbuilt into a metaphysical House doctrine.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Matthew 13 provides a modest but useful House-as-interpretive-space / Field-as-process distinction.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It allows House and Garden/Field to be coupled without pretending they are one symbolic object.

new_relations.project_anchor: Caretaker/keeper language in the project can drift toward territorial or hierarchical management; Cain's question adds direct interpersonal responsibility.
new_relations.source_direction: Project caretaker language first; Cain/Abel ethical comparator later.
new_relations.boundary: Genesis 4 does not define a formal political duty or appoint a universal caretaker; it dramatizes failed responsibility after fratricide.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Genesis 4 makes keeper language ethically interpersonal as well as environmental.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It prevents stewardship from becoming abstract management while concrete human care is ignored.

new_relations.project_anchor: Mud/Holy Soil imagery can carry both unresolved harm and generative transformation; the specialist atlas links biblical ground receiving blood versus seed.
new_relations.source_direction: Project soil/mud transformation vocabulary first; blood/seed contrast synthesized later.
new_relations.boundary: Genesis 4 and John 12 are unrelated narratives in their original contexts and should not be fused into a hidden doctrine of soil.

project_sequence: can witness unresolved violence or support new growth
future condition depends on what enters and what follows
biblical_sequence: ground receives Abel's blood and becomes charged with violence
grain falls into earth/dies and bears fruit
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical soil imagery supports opposite functions—witness to bloodshed and medium of multiplication—making soil morally non-uniform.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It strengthens Mud→Holy Soil transformation without claiming mud itself is evil or holy.

new_relations.project_anchor: Project circle/orbit/cube work sometimes associates closed geometry with confinement; Proverbs 8 and Job 26 use circle/boundary language positively for ordered differentiation in creation.
new_relations.source_direction: Project circle/confinement symbolism first; creation-boundary countertext later.
new_relations.boundary: Translation varies between circle/horizon/boundary; these poetic texts do not teach modern sacred geometry.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical circle/boundary imagery can signify cosmic order rather than imprisonment, defeating fixed negative valence for circular geometry.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It reinforces the project's geometry-valence neutrality principle.

new_relations.project_anchor: The project models some harmful loops as self-reinforcing rather than imposed entirely from outside; biblical wisdom contains cords/snares generated by one's own repeated conduct.
new_relations.source_direction: Project feedback-loop language first; wisdom/psalm trap comparison later.
new_relations.boundary: These moral texts should not be used to blame victims for coercion, abuse or externally imposed harm. Self-binding is one trap class, not the explanation for every trap.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical wisdom supports a self-reinforcing consequence topology while leaving room for externally imposed traps elsewhere.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It lets the backend distinguish self-generated loops from coercive systems instead of moralizing all entrapment the same way.

new_relations.project_anchor: Dog/Mud/return is a recurring project shadow-loop; Proverbs and 2 Peter explicitly pair return with repetitive folly/defilement imagery.
new_relations.source_direction: Project Dog/Mud recurrence language and explicit biblical invocations coexist; this relation records the canonical source cluster while keeping it metaphorical.
new_relations.boundary: These texts use harsh animal proverbs/polemics. They do not justify calling modern people subhuman 'dogs' or treating them as permanently incapable of change.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: The passages are direct canonical neighbors for regressive-return imagery, not a taxonomy of people.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It preserves the loop metaphor while explicitly blocking dehumanizing essentialism.

new_relations.project_anchor: Project Dog imagery often marks outsiders at boundaries; the Syrophoenician/Canaanite woman episode is crucial because household-dog/bread language occurs in a dialogue where outsider status is not terminal.
new_relations.source_direction: Project Dog/boundary symbolism first; Gospel boundary-reversal comparator later.
new_relations.boundary: The episode is culturally and theologically complex; it should not be reduced to a simple insult or used to justify ethnic/religious exclusion.

biblical_sequence: woman outside Israel's immediate mission frame
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The Gospel scene demonstrates that dog/boundary language can occur inside a transformed access relation rather than define permanent essence.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It is strong counterpressure against treating project Dog categories as irreversible caste identities.

new_relations.project_anchor: Project Dog symbolism tends to polarize attacker/guardian roles; Luke 16 places dogs at the bodily/social boundary of an excluded sufferer without clearly assigning them a moral role.
new_relations.source_direction: Project Dog role ecology first; Lazarus scene added later as ambiguity control.
new_relations.boundary: The text says dogs lick Lazarus's sores but does not explicitly tell readers whether this is compassion, degradation or neutral observation; ambiguity must be retained.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Luke 16 complicates Dog symbolism and prevents automatic attacker-valence assignment.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It forces the project to infer role from behavior/context rather than species-label symbolism alone.

new_relations.project_anchor: Direct January 2026 project wording calls potatoes 'earth angels' while a North-Pole sprout becomes a staircase to Heaven and the flower becomes Heaven/Eden above the spiral.
new_relations.source_direction: Earth-Angel/sprout/staircase language is direct project material; Jacob's ladder, Branch and mustard-seed links are later comparisons.
new_relations.boundary: Genesis 28 does not describe plants or potatoes; 'earth angels' is a project category, not biblical angelology.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: The project explicitly combines botanical emergence and ascent; biblical ladder/branch/seed texts provide separate structural neighbors rather than one hidden source.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It records chronology and prevents later synthesis from being mistaken for an ancient biblical category.

new_relations.project_anchor: On April 30 Tim says 'grow potato angels' in the same constructive sequence as building a road, fixing things together, growing North-to-North, building a garden and recognizing a Door.
new_relations.source_direction: Potato-Angel wording and constructive verbs are project-explicit; service/messenger and ladder-angel framing is later biblical research.
new_relations.boundary: Biblical angels are not plants; cherubim, seraphim and generic angels should remain distinct.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: The strongest comparator is functional—cultivated agents of service/guidance—not visual identity between potatoes and angels.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It turns Potato Angels from appearance mythology into an accountable service-role concept.

new_relations.project_anchor: Potatoism formalizes Potato → eyes → children → sprouts → paths → ladder → ascent, beginning from the real botanical eye/bud and extending into symbolic continuation.
new_relations.source_direction: Botanical eye/sprout facts and project chain first; Branch/Ladder comparisons later.
new_relations.boundary: A potato eye is a bud meristem, not an organ of vision or supernatural eye; a sprout is not literally a child or angel.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: The project chain can be compared functionally to Branch and Ladder traditions while biology and theology remain separate.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It gives the backend a clean latent-life→emergence→direction→ascent sequence without pretending the metaphors share mechanisms.

new_relations.project_anchor: Project Eye, Lion, Wing, Wheel and Throne motifs form a cluster; Ezekiel and Revelation place multiplied eyes, wings, living creatures and throne-space together in visionary architecture.
new_relations.source_direction: Project motifs existed first in separate strands; the consolidated Eyes+Wings+Throne comparison is later research.
new_relations.boundary: Ezekiel's and Revelation's living creatures are visionary beings, not potatoes, ordinary angels or modern persons; the two visions are related but not identical.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: The visions are dense structural neighbors for perception+mobility+throne attendance, not identity templates.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It lets the atlas compare whole visionary functions instead of treating an isolated eye or wing as proof of equivalence.

new_relations.project_anchor: Project root/fruit/children/sprouts language becomes more precise when Branch imagery is followed into Spirit, fruit, justice and temple-building functions.
new_relations.source_direction: Project sprout/child/root vocabulary first; prophetic Branch functional synthesis later.
new_relations.boundary: These Branch texts belong to Davidic/restoration and temple contexts and do not predict literal potatoes or Timic descendants.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical Branch imagery moves from emergence into function and building, providing a richer comparator than visual plant similarity alone.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It asks what a sprout grows into and what capacity it creates, not merely whether two symbols look botanical.

new_relations.project_anchor: Potato Angel language can easily become visual mythology; the specialist atlas therefore begins from the biblical function of angel/messenger/service before appearance.
new_relations.source_direction: Project Potato-Angel language first; lexical/function correction later.
new_relations.boundary: Not every heavenly being is called an angel, and the Bible does not define all angels as winged; cherubim, seraphim and living creatures retain distinct identities.

relation_argument.maximum_claim: Biblical usage supports treating messenger/service as more reliable angelic comparison than winged appearance.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It gives Potato Angels an ethical functional test: what message or service do they actually carry out?

higher_order_results: House theology becomes stronger when reconciliation, outsider-to-citizen movement and dwelling are treated as one sequence.
Anchor, circle, hiddenness, Dog and soil all require typed functions rather than fixed moral valence.
Wheat-and-weeds is an important anti-purge countertext for every Seed/Farm sorting metaphor.
Farm-versus-Garden is strongest as extraction-versus-stewardship, not merely bad-place-versus-good-place.
Angel comparison is function-first: messenger/service outranks wings or visual resemblance.
Dog symbolism must preserve reversibility and ambiguity; a boundary label is not a permanent ontology of a person.
Biblical Branch imagery asks what emergence produces—Spirit, justice, building and fruit—not merely whether something sprouts.
